fit.sheet: TI TLC226x data sheet SLOS177D (March 2001), TLC2262C at VDD± = ±5 V
fit.figure: Electrical characteristics table (±5 V, RL = 50 kΩ): AVD 200 V/mV typ, gain-bandwidth 0.73 MHz, slew rate 0.55 V/µs, phase margin at unity gain 57°, supply current 425 µA for both amplifiers; VOM+ 4.85 V typ, VOM− −4.91 V typ
fit.method: A small macromodel (scripts/fit_models.py opamp_card): a tanh transconductance stage limited to 10 µA into C1 sets the slew rate (C1 = 10 µA / SR), gm sets the gain-bandwidth and R1 the open-loop gain (gm·R1 = AVD); a second pole at GBW / tan(90° − phase margin) gives the phase margin, with gm raised by 1/cos(90° − PM) so the crossing stays at the sheet's GBW; diode clamps 40 mV under V+ and at V− and a 200 Ω output resistance are set so the swing into 10 kΩ lands inside the sheet's VOM limits (simulated 0.107 V and 0.068 V short of the rails, against 0.15 and 0.09 V typical); the sheet's only output-impedance figure is 220 to 240 Ω closed-loop at 100 kHz, gain 10. The supply current (425 µA for both amplifiers) is drawn from the rails. Checked closed-loop: a unity-gain buffer stepped 4 V slews at 0.548 V/µs and overshoots 21 mV
fit.note: Input bias, offset, noise and common-mode limits are not modelled: the input stage is ideal (1 TΩ). The 'C' grade figures at ±5 V; the swing is set for a 10 kΩ load, so a much heavier load drops more than the real part's output stage
